name: Pittsburg
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Pittsburg, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Pittsburg, CA: Twilight Holiday Parade, Old Town tree lighting, A Christmas Carol at the California Theatre and a Polar Express night.
lede: Pittsburg does Christmas in Old Town, where the city's Twilight Holiday Parade rolls down Railroad Avenue to the tree lighting, and the California Theatre and the Marina add holiday shows and family nights.
celebrates: The City of Pittsburg Recreation Department runs the Twilight Holiday Parade and Tree Lighting each December in Old Town, with floats, bands and children in costume walking down Railroad Avenue, and Santa arriving with the Pittsburg High School Marching Band. The community tree is lit after the parade. On the same street, the California Theatre hosts Pittsburg Theatre Company productions, including A Christmas Carol. City Recreation also runs holiday programs for children, such as a Polar Express themed Parents' Night Out at the Marina Community Center, and the Pittsburg Yacht Club holds a lighted boat parade at the marina.
lastyear: Pittsburg's 2025 Twilight Holiday Parade took place on Saturday, December 6, with Twilight as the theme. The parade started at 5 pm on Railroad Avenue, and the tree lighting followed. Afterward the city thanked the participants, the families who came out, the float builders and the marching groups, and gave a special thank you to the Pittsburg High School Marching Band for kicking off the parade. The Recreation Department posted a recap video and the list of 2025 parade winners on its website.
facts: Pittsburg has had three names. After coal was found in the southern foothills, the town became known as Black Diamond, a name first noted on local maps in 1868 because of the Black Diamond Coal Company. It incorporated as Black Diamond in 1903. Then, by popular vote on February 11, 1911, residents changed the name to Pittsburg, after the eastern city that was the birthplace of the steel industry. Today the holiday parade still runs through Old Town on Railroad Avenue.
trains: Pittsburg has two BART stations: Pittsburg/Bay Point, and Pittsburg Center, which opened on May 26, 2018, when BART extended service 10 miles east to Antioch. Amtrak trains stop next door at the Antioch-Pittsburg station, 100 I Street in Antioch. In Old Town, the main street where the holiday parade runs is Railroad Avenue. For a bigger train day in December, BART runs into San Francisco, home of the Cable Car Museum and the San Francisco Railway Museum.

kidfact: Pittsburg used to be called Black Diamond, because of the coal found in its hills. In 1911 the people voted to name it after Pittsburgh, the city famous for making steel.
faq: When is the Pittsburg holiday parade?

The City of Pittsburg Recreation Department holds the Twilight Holiday Parade and Tree Lighting in Old Town on a Saturday evening in early December. In 2025 it was on December 6, starting at 5 pm on Railroad Avenue, with the tree lighting after the parade. Groups apply ahead of time through the city to march or enter a float.
Where does the Pittsburg parade go?

The parade runs down Railroad Avenue in Old Town Pittsburg, with floats, bands and children in costume. The Pittsburg High School Marching Band escorts Santa down the avenue, and in 2025 the city thanked the band for kicking off the parade. The community tree lighting follows.
Can we take BART to Pittsburg?

Yes. Pittsburg has two BART stations: Pittsburg/Bay Point and Pittsburg Center, which opened in May 2018 with the 10 mile extension to Antioch. Amtrak trains stop at the Antioch-Pittsburg station at 100 I Street in Antioch, which serves both cities. From either BART station, trains run west toward Concord, Oakland and San Francisco.
Why is the city called Pittsburg?

The town was first known as Black Diamond, after the Black Diamond Coal Company, and incorporated under that name in 1903. On February 11, 1911, residents voted to rename it Pittsburg, after the eastern birthplace of the steel industry. The Pittsburg Historical Society museum tells more of the story.
